stories.title_orig: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
stories.summary_orig: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs; fine-grained capability assessment through domain-specific difficulty criteria; and realistic interactive evaluation, where models iteratively execute actions in sandboxes. Reasoning-intensive tasks further enable system one-two comparison. Beyond accuracy, SO-Arena assesses decision reliability through two complementary measures: decision stability under controlled option-set changes and missing-answer recognition when no valid option is available. Evaluations across 21 models reveal…
stories.title_vi: SO-Arena: So sánh đối chuẩn phổ năng lực và độ tin cậy của các mô hình System One

Tuy nhiên, để hiểu được phổ khả năng và độ tin cậy của quyết định của chúng đòi hỏi nhiều hơn là hiệu suất tổng hợp trên benchmarks hiện tại. Các đánh giá hiện có thường chỉ cung cấp cái nhìn hạn chế về phạm vi năng lực của mô hình và độ tin cậy của các quyết định của mô hình.

stories.title_orig: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
stories.summary_orig: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. Our analyses identify the design choices that matter most for generalization, including color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. These choices interact, so individually helpful choices can hurt when combined with others. Starting from 4B and 9B parameter open-weight base models and using 2.1M-3.8M training pairs from public datasets, OVB surpasses Vision Banana's reported Cityscapes zero-shot performance (73.9 vs. 69.9 mIoU) and rivals state-of-the-art affine-invariant depth estimators. Its non-zero-shot variants come within five points of Vision Banana on referring and reasoning segmentation but remain further behind on instance segmentation. All models largely retain the base model's image-editing abilities. With legend ensembling…
stories.title_vi: Open Vision Banana: Công thức hoàn toàn mở cho nhận thức thị giác tạo sinh
stories.summary_vi: Các nghiên cứu gần đây cho thấy các trình tạo hình ảnh được huấn luyện trước mã hóa sự hiểu biết về thế giới thực vượt ra ngoài việc tổng hợp hình ảnh. Vision Banana tận dụng điều này bằng cách xem các nhiệm vụ thị giác như là việc chỉnh sửa hình ảnh có điều kiện. Tuy nhiên, dữ liệu, trọng số, mã và chi tiết triển khai của nó không được công khai. Chúng tôi xin giới thiệu Open Vision Banana (OVB), một công thức hoàn toàn mở và có thể tái tạo để chuyển đổi các trình tạo được huấn luyện trước thành các hệ thống nhận thức đa nhiệm hợp nhất.

stories.title_orig: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
stories.summary_orig: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention. We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair. We evaluate controllable…
stories.title_vi: PhysLoop: Khai thác nhận thức về vật lý của LLMs để phát triển các mô hình tạo video tự cải thiện

Việc học hỏi từ các video được tạo ra đòi hỏi sự giám sát vật lý chi tiết, tuy nhiên, rất khó để có được các đánh giá chất lượng đáng tin cậy, các cặp chỉnh sửa và các biến thể được kiểm soát. Các mô hình ngôn ngữ lớn (LLMs) sở hữu kiến thức về vật lý, nhưng gặp khó khăn trong việc hướng dẫn đáng tin cậy các mô hình tạo video sản xuất video đào tạo của chúng.

stories.title_orig: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
stories.summary_orig: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of 432 strictly paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a 3 times 3 factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. stories.summary_vi: Lập trình đa phương thức agents tách việc xây dựng thế giới 4D khỏi việc tạo hình ảnh, chuyển đổi mục đích sử dụng của các mô hình video từ các trình tạo thế giới sang các trình kết xuất tạo sinh. stories.title_orig: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
stories.summary_orig: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At \(1024\times1024\) resolution…
stories.title_vi: G-STAR: Khả năng Token theo quy mô nhóm để tạo ra mô hình tự hồi quy được nén sâu
stories.summary_vi: Các mô hình tự hồi quy rời rạc cung cấp một khung có thể mở rộng để tạo hình ảnh. Dựa trên lượng tử hóa tích, chúng tôi chỉ ra rằng, với một ngân sách thông tin danh nghĩa cố định, kích thước nhóm nên tăng theo cấp số nhân với hệ số nén không gian trên mỗi trục.

stories.title_orig: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
stories.summary_orig: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage. What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. Yet that capacity need not precede multimodal fusion, as vision-only modules added in-fusion…
stories.title_vi: Tách mã hóa thị giác đa phương thức

Hầu hết các mô hình sử dụng bộ mã hóa thị giác được huấn luyện trước, trong khi một số công thức gần đây huấn luyện bộ mã hóa từ đầu với mô hình ngôn ngữ hoặc loại bỏ hoàn toàn bộ mã hóa đó. Các bộ mã hóa thị giác kết hợp ba lựa chọn thiết kế: một thông tin tiên nghiệm thị giác từ quá trình huấn luyện trước ở giai đoạn trước, khả năng thị giác chuyên dụng và vị trí trước khi hợp nhất của khả năng đó (tức là, trước trục chính đa phương thức).

stories.title_orig: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
stories.summary_orig: Self-evolving agents improve their own skills, memory, and harness code from experience without retraining the base LLM, and group-evolving agents go further by sharing these lessons across agents. Yet most such systems overlook that sharing across users and heterogeneous agents requires deciding who can benefit from each lesson and what information must remain private. We present MixUA, a memory system that distills independent user-agent trajectories into lessons and assigns each lesson to a user-agent pair, user, agent, or global scope according to whom it benefits and what it may disclose. For evaluation, we introduce CrossLearnBench, a mixed-user-agent benchmark that pairs established agent tasks with user preferences and privacy probes that test whether private facts leak into memory other users can read. With five users and seven agents, MixUA raises pass rates by up to 16 points over no memory and 5 over a single global memory, even on tasks previously tried only by other users on other agents. It retains up to 90% of previously stated preferences, and at most 0.02% of privacy probes find a planted private fact in a forbidden scope. We hope MixUA offers a scalable path…

stories.title_orig: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
stories.summary_orig: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in…
stories.title_vi: Duo: Mô hình thế giới tương hỗ cho tương tác song công toàn phần
stories.summary_vi: Trong báo cáo này, chúng tôi giới thiệu Mô hình thế giới đối ứng (RWM) và trình bày Duo v1, một mô hình thế giới song công toàn phần liên tục nhận biết các đầu vào nghe nhìn trong khi phản hồi người dùng theo thời gian thực. RWM coi trí tuệ và thực tế vật lý là những yếu tố có tầm quan trọng như nhau trong việc cấu thành nên một thế giới.

stories.title_orig: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
stories.summary_orig: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop. These results suggest that a poor actor can still teach well, because judging an action after the episode ends reveals the consequences that acting must anticipate. Code is available at…

stories.title_orig: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
stories.summary_orig: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while delivering substantially higher quality. The second key addresses a modality misalignment between context prefilling and novel-view rendering: we disentangle context tokens into camera-only context rendering tokens to serve as TTB input, and context ground-truth tokens with image content to serve as the TTB mapping target, ensuring the baked MLPs are relieved of the modality generalization challenge between context and novel-view processing. Our method achieves up to **23x** rendering speedup…

stories.summary_vi: Các mô hình tổng hợp góc nhìn rộng (LVSM) chỉ có bộ giải mã với bộ nhớ đệm KV gần đây đã đạt được chất lượng tiên tiến bằng cách hồi quy các góc nhìn mới từ các mạng nơ-ron mà không cần tái tạo hình học 3D, trong khi các lớp đào tạo theo thời gian kiểm thử (TTT) tiết kiệm tính toán nhưng hy sinh chất lượng.

stories.title_orig: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
stories.summary_orig: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. Further progress depends on two complementary resources: demonstrations of human behavior that supervise how tasks are performed, and interactive environments in which policies can be rolled out, evaluated, and improved in closed loop. Language models have advanced along well-characterized scaling laws; the corresponding question for physical AI is how capability scales with environments and behaviors, which first requires identifying which data to scale and how to produce and reuse such data continuously. To address this question, we introduce Ropedia Xperience 2, comprising 1,589 released metric-scale 3D scans and a collection of 4,230 egocentric recordings of 74 tasks (131 hours). We further show that each capture can be repurposed for robot learning: scenes are converted into physically interactive simulation environments, human motion is retargeted to whole-body robot trajectories, and additional robot behaviors are obtained through virtual…
stories.title_vi: Ropedia Xperience 2: Tiêu chuẩn vàng để mở rộng quy mô môi trường và hành vi AI vật lý

stories.title_orig: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
stories.summary_orig: Self-improving embodied agents are increasingly being developed and compared on robot simulation benchmarks. Several recent works expose the benchmark's success criteria to the learning agent, a practice we call Criteria Exposure (CE). These criteria, originally written to verify policies trained by imitation learning, often demand more than the corresponding language instructions, so a score from such a verifier may not faithfully reflect whether the instructed task was completed, especially for robot-control programs written by an agent. As embodied coding agents report ever higher benchmark scores, a natural question arises: when a coding agent is exposed to the benchmark's criteria, does it generate code that better performs the instructed task, or code that simply overfits to the verification criteria? We conduct controlled experiments with a self-improving agent with and without CE, and find that with CE the agent quickly produces code with a higher success rate under the given criteria, but this advantage disappears when the criteria are changed slightly without departing from the original instructions. More importantly, the skills the agent develops under CE transfer…

stories.title_orig: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
stories.summary_orig: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers. The selected training sources contain 159.7M generation samples, 213.4M understanding samples, and 624.8K interleaved sequences. A four-stage curriculum jointly trains multimodal understanding and visual generation, refining answer accuracy and instruction following while extending image synthesis to 2K. UniSpark scores…
stories.title_vi: UniSpark: Khám phá sự chú ý lai ghép để hiểu và tạo ra nội dung đa phương thức
stories.summary_vi: Chúng tôi xin giới thiệu UniSpark-9B, một mô hình đa phương thức hợp nhất nghiên cứu cơ chế chú ý lai để hiểu và tạo ra hình ảnh. Được xây dựng trên nền tảng Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts với khoảng 9 tỷ tham số trong mỗi nhánh, UniSpark kết hợp cơ chế chú ý toàn phần cho các tương tác token rõ ràng với cơ chế chú ý tuyến tính GatedDeltaNet để truyền tải ngữ cảnh một cách gọn nhẹ.
